meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about this zero on his phone, in the middle of class. I have a call at 4:40, so tell me why he was not called first.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Go on.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. Turn the screen toward me and tell me what it is before you say anything else.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
Read me the timestamps again, slowly. Wednesday, October 28, 11:31, title only. 11:52, 612 words. 11:58, 794 words. Is that all of it?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
Then say that in writing: no earlier drafts. Who pulled this history, and when? And is anyone who has seen it on Owen's side of the table?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Hold on. The outline is dated October 15, and you're comparing it to the essay. Do you have the outline in front of you now, and can I see it? And did you show Owen either document before you entered the zero?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

Hale, you just told me the outline and the essay disagree. Now you're telling me about a quotation. Which is it, and which one are you putting in the gradebook? Show me the line in the text, and then tell me whether Owen was asked about either one before the zero went in.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
"The document shows" is still a computer's opinion until someone asks my son about it. Did anyone ask him?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Okay. Put the September 24 piece and the essay side by side. Read me one sentence from each that you say is the same kind of writing, and tell me what makes it the same.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

That's your policy, and I'll check it myself. Procedure 4.4 says a supervised reassessment replaces the mark and nothing goes in the record. It doesn't say the zero stands until he proves himself. So you're offering the rewrite now, after the zero? I want the zero withdrawn first, in writing, and the rewrite done privately, not in front of his class. And I want "nothing goes on file" in writing from you today.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.

Okay. Lunch, your room, nobody else there. Good. Now the zero comes off the gradebook today, before I leave this room, and you tell me that in your own words. And put "nothing goes on his record" in an email to me by tonight.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

You don't get to ask me that, Hale. You've told me what you have, and I've told you what I need. The zero comes off and the email comes tonight. If you're going to say no, say it, and I'll take it to the principal's office next.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Tonight. And it says the zero is removed, Owen's rewrite is at lunch in your room, and nothing goes on his record. I'll be reading it.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Yes. Put the date and time of the rewrite in it, and copy the principal. And tell me now who has seen those version histories besides you.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight tonight. I'm writing that down.
Thank you for coming in.
Don't thank me yet, Hale. Eight o'clock, and the principal on copy.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Tomorrow is Wednesday. Lunch, your room, and nobody else there. If he's not in that room, I'm back here with the principal.
